title: Parking fee for heavy cars (SUVs)
titleFr: Tarif de stationnement pour les voitures lourdes (SUV)
summary: Should visitors' heavy cars pay triple for street parking in Paris? A real votation (4 Feb 2024): we compare the simulated voters with the official result by sector — and show who pays but cannot vote.
proposalFr: La Ville de Paris organise une votation citoyenne le 4 février 2024. Question : « Pour ou contre la création d'un tarif spécifique pour le stationnement des voitures individuelles lourdes, encombrantes, polluantes ? » Si le « Pour » l'emporte, le stationnement en surface des voitures de visiteurs pesant au moins 1,6 tonne (thermiques ou hybrides rechargeables) ou au moins 2 tonnes (électriques) coûtera 18 € de l'heure dans les arrondissements centraux (1er au 11e) et 12 € de l'heure dans les autres (12e au 20e), soit trois fois le tarif actuel. Ne seraient pas concernés : les Parisiens qui se garent dans leur zone de stationnement résidentiel, les artisans et professionnels munis d'une carte professionnelle, les taxis et les personnes en situation de handicap. (Une position favorable (+) signifie voter « Pour » ce tarif.)
proposalEn: Paris citizens' vote, 4 Feb 2024: 'For or against a specific parking rate for heavy, bulky, polluting individual cars?' If 'For' wins, on-street parking for visitors' cars of 1.6 t or more (combustion/plug-in hybrid) or 2 t or more (electric) costs €18/h in arrondissements 1–11 and €12/h in 12–20, three times today's price. Exempt: Parisians parking in their residential zone, tradespeople with a professional card, taxis and disabled drivers.

leakage.notes: Leakage probe pending API key (run pipeline/leakage_probe.py). Model-card pretraining cutoffs: Nemotron 3 Nano 2025-06-25, Nemotron 3 Super 2025-06, Nemotron 3 Ultra 2025-09; vote date 2024-02-04. All three Nemotron 3 models were pre-trained on data up to at least June 2025, after this vote: treat the backtest as possibly contaminated and run the leakage probe.

poll.org: OpinionWay for Respire and Clean Cities
poll.note: NOT the ballot question: 61 % support parking charges based on vehicle weight (70 % if conditions such as reinvesting revenue and exempting residents apply). Commissioned by groups campaigning FOR the measure. Sample of 1,019 people aged 18+, online (CAWI).

uncertainty.method: K=3 proposal paraphrases × 2 models (NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B, nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b) on a random 300-resident subsample; yesRange = full-sample yes share shifted by the min/max deviation of the runs from the main run on that subsample (MOCK: seeded noise, not real model variation)

notes: MOCK RUN: no language model was called (no API key). Stances and texts come from simple deterministic heuristics and templates marked [demo]/[démo].
Every text is a simulated voice generated for a synthetic resident, never a real person. Results are hypotheses to test, not evidence of public opinion.

Participation: logit(p) = logit(participationBase or participationPropensity) + 0.35·exposure + 0.5·(LLM self-report − 0.5) + c, with c = -4.019 calibrated so expected participants = 5.68% of the 1082 residents in scope. The LLM self-report is only a weak rank modifier. The highlighted attendees on the map are one seeded random draw; all attendee numbers use the probability weights.

Neighbour talk: 280 random pairs (214 within 300 m, the rest in the same district); 64 of 560 residents changed stance. Arguments that travelled most: Big cars are dangerous and take up space (87); Cleaner air and more street space (60); Another cost for households who need a big car (60).
The OpinionWay for Respire and Clean Cities poll did not ask the ballot question, so it is shown for context only: no gap-sign test and no 'uniform poll' baseline for this vote.
Does talking help? Sector MAE 0.165 before talk vs 0.161 after (more accurate).

Backtest rules: participation coefficients, turnout target (= official turnout) and the demographic baseline were fixed before comparing with sector results; nothing is tuned on the vote being predicted.
Imputed attributes (car, heavy car, tenure, nationality, workplace) come from INSEE statistics, not from the NVIDIA dataset, and are labelled as imputed.
